chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding a man who bequeathed more than the third, and emancipated his slave during his illness, he said: If it was more than the third, return it to the third, and the emancipation is valid.

key_terms.الثُّلُث: The third (one-third share of the estate)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bequeathing more than one-third of an estate in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the interaction between the 'one-third' limit for bequests and the validity of manumission during final illness (marad al-mawt). It establishes that while excess bequests are reduced to the one-third share to protect heirs' rights, the act of freeing a slave is treated as a distinct, valid transaction that is not subject to the same reduction, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the independence of manumission from the general bequest cap.
